body.hook: Billie Eilish and her brother Finneas recorded her first album in a small bedroom with a laptop. Today, a digital audio workstation (DAW) is a recording studio, a band and a mixing desk in one app.

study.title: Loop Lab
study.question: How do producers build a track from loops?
study.passage:
Tools: a free DAW such as BandLab, GarageBand or Soundtrap, plus headphones.
Part 1, Tour (10 minutes): Find the transport controls (play, stop, record), the timeline, track list, loop browser, tempo and key settings, mixer (volume and pan), and export.
Part 2, Set up (5 minutes): New project at 90 to 120 bpm, in one key.
Part 3, Build (25 minutes): Choose four loops: drums, bass, chords and a melody or vocal chop. Arrange a 32-bar track:
Intro (8 bars): chords only
Section A (8 bars): add drums and bass
Section B (8 bars): add melody; change one loop for contrast
Outro (8 bars): remove parts one by one
Part 4, Balance (5 minutes): Adjust volumes so drums and melody are clear; pan one part slightly left and one slightly right.
Part 5, Export (5 minutes): Export as MP3 and name it "Name_Track1."
Copyright note: Built-in loops in these DAWs are royalty-free; samples from commercial songs are not.

items.q: What does DAW stand for?
items.answer: Digital audio workstation.

items.q: Define loop.
items.answer: A short musical pattern that repeats seamlessly.

items.q: Explain why loops must share key and tempo.
items.answer: So they fit together harmonically and rhythmically.

items.q: Describe the structure of your 32-bar track.
items.answer: Answers vary; intro, A, B, outro.

items.q: What is panning and why use it?
items.answer: Placing sounds left or right to create space and clarity.

items.q: How long is a 16-bar section at 120 bpm in 4/4?
items.answer: 32 seconds.

items.q: Explain how adding and removing layers creates shape in a track.
items.answer: Changing the number of parts raises or lowers energy across sections.

items.q: Explain why built-in loops are safe but song samples may not be.
items.answer: Built-in loops are licensed royalty-free; commercial samples are copyrighted.
